Normalize function-invoke headers and introduce tool-selection backoff policy for OpenAI-compat

Context: We need stronger OpenAI-compat behavior for function/tool invocation metadata without changing user-facing API shapes. Previously the OpenAI adapter sent ad-hoc metadata in the streaming envelope which caused downstream consumers (proxies and third-party SDKs) to misinterpret tool selection cues and header ordering, leading to flaky tool handoffs during scaled traffic spikes. Motivation: unify invocation headers so the compat layer emits a canonical header set and introduce an exponential backoff policy when tool selection is congested to reduce duplicate/competing invocations and improve end-to-end stability.
Normalize: canonicalize invoke headers and add header-v2 schema
Runtime: honor header priority when framing streaming messages
Policy: implement tool-selection backoff controller and tests
Docs: add migration notes and example payloads for clients
Tests: integration tests for backoff and header preservation in retries
Amit Shah: Can we avoid changing the wire header name for existing clients? Suggest adding a versioned X-Redwood-Invoke header and preserving the old one for a deprecation window.
Carla Nguyen: Addressed — added X-Redwood-Invoke-V2 and mirror to X-Redwood-Invoke for one release. Kept mapping deterministic so proxies can upgrade smoothly.
Lena Ortiz: Backoff parameters look sane but add observability: counters for backoff triggers and per-tool contention gauge.
Carla Nguyen: Added metrics hooks and dashboard snippet in docs. Also tightened default max backoff from 10s to 5s per infra feedback.
Marcus Lee: Integration test failed on first CI run due to race in stream_framer; fixed by moving header normalization earlier in the pipeline.
CI Bot: rerun required after addressing flake in stream framing tests. All checks passed on rerun.
- OpenAI-compat: invoke header schema v2 (X-Redwood-Invoke-V2). The adapter mirrors v2 to the legacy header during a deprecation window.
- Stability: tool-selection controller now backs off competing handoffs on contention to reduce duplicate tool invocations and improve routing stability.
- Observability: new metrics redwood.tool_selection.backoff.count and redwood.tool_selection.contention.gauge

Clients: no immediate change required. Optional: switch to reading X-Redwood-Invoke-V2 to obtain structured invoke metadata (JSON object encoded as base64). The legacy X-Redwood-Invoke will be removed after two releases; watch redwood-announce for schedule.
Backport to release/2025-11 required for some enterprise clusters using private deploy. The header mirroring avoids immediate client changes but operations teams should schedule client SDK updates to consume v2 cleanly.
Small CPU overhead (~1-2%) from header normalization and backoff controller; expected reduction in wasted concurrent tool invocations under contention, improving overall tail latency during spikes.
If you see increased backoff counts, check tool capacity and routing policies. Emergency rollback: revert the feature flag compat.invoke_headers_v2 and disable tool_selection_backoff via runtime feature gate.
Header v2 example: X-Redwood-Invoke-V2: eyJ0b29sIjoi/qa-tool
Invoke payload example in docs: {"tool":"qa-tool","version":"1.3","memo":"trimmed"} (encoded)
